title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 212 (Skill and diligence required from agent)

content.overview: An agent is bound to conduct the business of the agency with as much skill as is generally possessed by persons engaged in similar business, unless the principal has notice of his want of skill. The agent is always bound to act with reasonable diligence, and to use such skill as he possesses; and to make compensation to his principal in respect of the direct consequences of his own neglect, want of skill or misconduct, but not in respect of loss or damage which are indirectly or remotely caused by such neglect, want of skill or misconduct.
content.glance: Skill of persons in similar business (unless principal knows of want of skill); always reasonable diligence; compensate for direct consequences of neglect/want of skill/misconduct.

sections.heading: Skill of similar business
sections.body: Skill generally possessed by persons in similar business, unless principal has notice of want of skill.

sections.heading: Always reasonable diligence
sections.body: Always bound to act with reasonable diligence and to use such skill as he possesses.

sections.heading: Compensation for direct consequences
sections.body: Compensate for direct consequences of neglect, want of skill or misconduct; not for remote loss.

provisions.title: Skill and diligence required from agent

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 212 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Test skill standard and notice of want of skill; test reasonable diligence; limit compensation to direct consequences.

examTips: Direct vs remote consequences; skill of similar business.
